question: Should OpenClaw core accept model-elected continuation tools and delegate returns as a first-party opt-in lifecycle feature at this breadth?
rationale: The PR adds new core tools, persisted flow state, plugin SDK boundary behavior, Codex integration behavior, and cross-session/session-state semantics that require maintainer intent rather than a mechanical repair decision.

options.title: Require exact-head proof and owner acceptance
options.body: Keep the PR open until the branch is mergeable and maintainers accept the product/security boundary with exact-head live proof for the remaining compaction success path.

options.title: Split the feature
options.body: Ask the contributor to split continuation, delegation, compaction, protocol/docs, and SDK hardening into smaller reviewable PRs with independent proof.

options.title: Accept as experimental opt-in
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the broad opt-in surface with the current proof caveats and own the upgrade/security risk.

recommendation.title: Require exact-head proof and owner acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until the branch is mergeable and maintainers accept the product/security boundary with exact-head live proof for the remaining compaction success path.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sampled current-main history across task-flow, system-event, and agent-runner surfaces touched by the feature.
